newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Philips's Brazil 1996 sales seen up 18 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philips's Brazil 1996 sales seen up 18 pct.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV's Brazilian unit Philips do Brasil estimates sales will reach $1.8 billion in 1996, a rise of 18.3 percent over a year ago, a company spokesman said.
The company has also increased by 35 percent sales volume this year, with TVs and stereo sales accounting for 47 percent of its total revenues, said the spokesman.
The company plans to invest $160 million in Brazil in 1997 to produce 100 new electrical appliance models. "We will modernize our production line and launch new products," the spokesman said.
Brazil accounts for 70 percent of all Philips' sales in South America.

According to Brazil's Electrical and Electronic Industry Association (Abinee), electrical appliance sales are likely to hit $12.9 billion in 1996, continuing to benefit from an on-going consumption wave which began after the government implemented its Real anti-inflation plan in mid-1994.
Next year appliance sales are projected to rise 10 percent, Abinee said.
